biography:
Michelle David & The True-Tones is a Dutch soul band featuring American vocalist Michelle David, raised in New York where she began singing gospel in church at age four and performed with The Mission of Love by five. After touring globally with Broadway productions like Mama, The Sound of Motown, Glory of Gospel, and Mahalia, and recording with artists such as Diana Ross and Michael Bolton, she settled in the Netherlands. There, she teamed up with Dutch musicians Paul Willemsen (guitar, bass), Onno Smit (guitar, bass), and Bas Bouma (drums), initially as a project exploring gospel roots of rhythm & blues and soul, evolving into a tight-knit band blending gospel, soul, blues, jazz, afrobeat, and more.

The band's sound is defined by groovy basslines, powerhouse vocals, and a fusion of classic soul with contemporary and global influences like Afrofunk, Calypso, Moroccan Gnawa, Brazilian flavors, and 70s indie vibes, earning them acclaim as one of Europe's most dynamic live acts. They have released at least seven critically acclaimed albums, including gospel-infused works, a Christmas album, Brothers & Sisters, and Truth & Soul (2022), with honors like a Dutch Edison Award nomination, BBC Radio 6 Album of the Year, and FIP Radio Album of the Month.

Their significance lies in reinventing gospel and soul traditions into vibrant, empowering spectacles, headlining festivals like Pinkpop, North Sea Jazz, and Veszprém Blues, performing at the 2022 Winter Olympics, and selling out shows worldwide, all while overcoming personal challenges like Michelle David's breast cancer diagnosis to continue trailblazing as "Holland's best soul singer.
